subject: [Glimmer AI] High 5xx rate from polarisx-small — interim mitigation & next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodeval.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@glimmer.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodeval.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 22:18:00 -0700
Subject: High 5xx rate from polarisx-small — immediate mitigation

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the heads-up in the dashboard. We see a sustained increase in 5xx and timeouts for requests routed to polarisx-small for your account over the last ~40 minutes. We’re actively triaging — initial findings from our edge are: 

- Error type: 503 + upstream timeouts, concentrated on the 512-token path.
- Scope: ~12% of your requests in last 30m (spike localized to cluster-us-west-2a).
- Impact: elevated latencies and failed responses for short synchronous calls (webhook flows).

Immediate actions we’re taking now: 
1) Fallback routing: we’ve enabled a temporary policy to route Glimmer's production traffic to polarisx-small-fallback (validated smaller-context variant) to reduce error surface.
2) Increased concurrency limits on the affected cluster to flush queued requests.
3) Captured debug logs and a sample trace bundle (attached).

ETA for full stabilization: target is 2–3 hours; will update sooner if the spike drops. We will also prepare a short postmortem and a timeline once we have root cause.

Short-term ask from your side: please confirm if you can tolerate the fallback model for the next 2–4 hours (it has the same tokenizer but slightly lower throughput for very long contexts). If you prefer not to use fallback, we’ll prioritize capacity rebalancing instead.

Attachments: glimmer-polarisx-503-sample-logs-20270518.tar.gz (log bundle), polarisx-small-fallback-configs.txt

Apologies for the interruption — we’re treating this as a priority.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwoodeval.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@glimmer.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 00:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: High 5xx rate from polarisx-small — immediate mitigation

Team — looped you in to confirm internal actions and approval for customer communication + any credits. Quick notes from triage: 

- Root cause (preliminary): an optimizer regression in a recently rolled kernel set for polarisx-small that increased tail latency under certain sequence-length distributions. The rollback candidate passes unit/regression tests but we need a staged rollout to avoid collateral.
- Current state: fallback routing is live for Glimmer; error rate for their traffic dropped from ~12% -> ~0.6% after routing change.
- Attachments: sample logs and trace link above; I added an incident Jira INC-2391.

Proposed customer-facing timeline (sendable after we validate rollback):
- 00:00–02:00: maintain fallback routing, monitor p95/p99.
- 02:00–03:00: staged rollback of the kernel change in cluster-us-west-2a (canary + gradual ramp).
- Post-rollback: 24h observation window and provide a formal postmortem within 72 hours.

Customer ask: confirm whether we can offer a goodwill credit for the incident window (recommended 5% of May invoice) — Ben, can you approve a credit for Glimmer if needed? Lauren, please prepare standard CS messaging and credits flow; I’ll attach the final postmortem draft.

Thanks —
Soojin

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodeval.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@glimmer.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodeval.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodeval.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodeval.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Glimmer incident update — rollback complete and postmortem summary

Hi Priya — final update and next steps. Thank you for your patience and the quick coordination with your SRE.

Summary:
- Timeline: cause identified and staged rollback executed in us-west-2a (complete at 07:10 PDT on 2027-05-19).
- Impact window: ~2027-05-18T21:35:00–2027-05-19T00:45:00 PDT (approx 3h10m).
- Root cause (final): a kernel optimization intended to improve batched attention performance regressed on a specific micro-batch size used by polarisx-small lead to unhandled timeouts in our kernel scheduler under high short-sequence concurrency.
- Mitigation: rollback to previous kernel, increased monitoring on micro-batch histograms, and enabled conservative scheduler thresholds for polarisx-small.
- Customer impact: ~6% of requests failed or timed out during the window; we observed a ~180ms increase in p95 for a subset of long-context requests prior to mitigation.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-glimmer-20270520.pdf (draft).

Action items & commitments:
1) Engineering: add a regression test for the micro-batch size distribution and a pre-deploy Canary that exercises the 512-token path (owner: Rishi, ETA: 2 weeks).
2) Runtime: add an automatic fallback policy for polarisx-small when queue depth exceeds threshold (owner: Soojin, ETA: 1 week).
3) CS/Finance: Ben and Lauren to coordinate a goodwill credit of 5% for May usage and confirm the billing adjustment by 2027-05-25.
4) Follow-up postmortem: formalized report to be delivered within 72 hours; we’ll include token-level metrics and the exact test vectors.

If you’d like a quick 30-minute bridge to go through the postmortem and the logs we attached, we can set that up — otherwise I’ll send the final report by Monday.

Apologies again for the disruption. We’re tracking this internally as a high-priority reliability improvement.

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwoodeval.com
